steps.subject: [InstCombine] Conditionally fold select i1 into and/or

evidence: Changes production InstCombine select-to-and/or formation, which directly changes BinaryOperator expression shapes seen by later simplification and analysis.
Poison-sensitive shift and logical-condition tests are somewhat adjacent to ValueTracking operand reasoning, but no getInvertibleOperand code is touched.
features: binary-operators, boolean-and-or, instcombine, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine, path:llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This InstCombine implementation change restricts conversion of i1 selects into and/or forms when unsafe select transforms are enabled. visitSelectInst now centralizes the decision in IsSafeToConvert: it still permits an arm that is implied poison under the condition, but otherwise rejects the fold for operators that can create poison or propagate poison from a directly poison-creating operator operand. The accompanying tests update expected output to retain selects in poison-sensitive cases.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitSelectInst; IsSafeToConvert; impliesPoison; canCreatePoison; propagatesPoison; foo1_and_signbit_lshr_without_shifting_signbit_logical; test1_logical; oneuse_shl_ashr_logical
Behavioral change: Replaces the previous unsafe-enabled condition, which accepted select-to-and/or folding without additional poison checks, with IsSafeToConvert for both the true-one and false-zero select forms.; When EnableUnsafeSelectTransform is enabled, blocks the fold if the nonconstant arm itself can create poison.; Also blocks the fold when that arm propagates poison and one of its direct operator operands can create poison.; Changes affected test expectations from and/or back to select forms, including cases containing shifts whose inputs can produce poison.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; canCreatePoison; propagatesPoison; impliesPoison; No direct retrieved reference to ValueTracking; No direct retrieved reference to getInvertibleOperand or BO1->getOperand
Reproducer link: The updated tests involve i1 selects, integer shifts, comparisons, and logical lowering; these are plausible sources of BinaryOperator and/or nodes.; No retrieved test reproduces the PR49535 compact C crash or the reported ValueTracking assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; i1 select-to-and/or canonicalization; poison-safety analysis
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate of the three because it changes InstCombine's creation of i1 and/or BinaryOperators, and the reported trace names a BinaryOperator operand together with InstCombine and ValueTracking invertible-operand reasoning. In particular, the commit changes whether poison-producing shift-derived conditions become logical operators. However, the shown code neither calls nor modifies getInvertibleOperand or ValueTracking, so the connection is indirect rather than a demonstrated assertion path.
Causal confidence: 0.25
Build risk: Modifies production InstCombine logic in visitSelectInst and changes optimization output for poison-sensitive i1 expressions.; The new safety predicate depends on canCreatePoison and propagatesPoison classification of operator trees.; A visible test adds a TODO stating that a related logical transform should be fixed using freeze, indicating remaining poison-semantics sensitivity.

selected_hunks.patch:
diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/pr49688.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/pr49688.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0de6a7f67b07
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/pr49688.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt < %s -instcombine -S | FileCheck %s
+
+define i1 @f(i32 %i1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @f(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SHR:%.*]] = lshr i32 7, [[I1:%.*]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[SHR]], [[I1]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[TMP0]]
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp = icmp slt i32 %i1, 0
+  %shr = ashr i32 7, %i1
+  %cmp4 = icmp sgt i32 %i1, %shr
+  %i2 = select i1 %cmp, i1 true, i1 %cmp4
+  ret i1 %i2
+}
+
+define i32 @f2(i32 signext %g, i32 zeroext %h) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @f2(
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SHR:%.*]] = lshr i32 7, [[H:%.*]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[SHR]], [[G:%.*]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOR_EXT:%.*]] = zext i1 [[TMP1]] to i32
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[LOR_EXT]]
+;
+  %cmp = icmp slt i32 %g, 0
+  %shr = ashr i32 7, %h
+  %cmp1 = icmp sgt i32 %g, %shr
+  %.0 = select i1 %cmp, i1 true, i1 %cmp1
+  %lor.ext = zext i1 %.0 to i32
+  ret i32 %lor.ext
+}

Summary: This commit adds InstCombine regression tests for scalable-vector/SVE IR only. The new tests cover shrinking an fpext/fadd/fptrunc splat sequence, scalable truncation and alloca casts, and preserving scalable-vector bitcasts of insertelement values rather than folding them into scalar bitcasts.
Changed symbols: shrink_splat_scalable_extend; trunc_nxv2i64_to_nxv2i32; bitcast_of_insert_i8_i16
Behavioral change: Adds test coverage asserting that InstCombine shrinks a scalable floating-point splat calculation to a float fadd.; Adds test coverage for scalable-vector truncation and fixed/scalable alloca bitcasts.; Adds tests requiring InstCombine not to fold bitcast(insertelement <vscale x 1 x i16>, ...) into a bitcast directly from i16, for both undef and poison insertelement bases.; The retrieved first-parent hunks contain no implementation, ValueTracking, or analysis-helper change.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is exercised by every new test; No retrieved hunk references ValueTracking; No retrieved hunk references getInvertibleOperand; No retrieved hunk references BO1->getOperand
Reproducer link: The tests use scalable-vector casts, shuffles, and SVE intrinsics rather than the compact scalar C -O2 reproducer described for PR49535.; No test reproduces an assertion or compiler crash.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; scalable-vector/SVE test coverage
Causal explanation: The commit is in the relevant InstCombine test tree, but its first-parent changes are exclusively new tests for scalable-vector canonicalizations. There is no compiler implementation change that could introduce the reported ValueTracking assertion, and the covered transformations do not show invertible-operand reasoning.

evidence: Introduces a substantive arithmetic InstCombine rewrite from shift comparisons to source range checks.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This change extends `InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant` to fold comparisons of a shifted value against zero even when the shift has multiple uses. For a zero constant, equality is rewritten to an unsigned-less-than comparison of the original operand against `(C + 1) << ShAmtVal`, while the non-equality path is rewritten to an unsigned-greater-than comparison against that threshold minus one. The accompanying first-parent test updates expect direct range comparisons for existing multiuse `lshr` and `ashr` cases.

diff --git a/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineCompares.cpp b/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineCompares.cpp
index fda87286fb38..4e3ddae9023e 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineCompares.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineCompares.cpp
@@ -2276,0 +2277,10 @@ Instruction *InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant(ICmpInst &Cmp,
+  if (C.isNullValue()) {
+    // == 0 is u< 1.
+    if (Pred == CmpInst::ICMP_EQ)
+      return new ICmpInst(CmpInst::ICMP_ULT, X,
+                          ConstantInt::get(ShrTy, (C + 1).shl(ShAmtVal)));
+    else
+      return new ICmpInst(CmpInst::ICMP_UGT, X,
+                          ConstantInt::get(ShrTy, (C + 1).shl(ShAmtVal) - 1));
+  }
+

Summary: This commit generalizes InstCombine's multiplication-overflow-check fold from unsigned division only to both unsigned and signed division. It renames the helper accordingly, extends the compare matcher to retain the matched division instruction and accept m_IDiv, and selects either llvm.umul.with.overflow or llvm.smul.with.overflow based on whether the matched division is UDiv or SDiv.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldUnsignedMultiplicationOverflowCheck; InstCombinerImpl::foldMultiplicationOverflowCheck; InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpBinOp; InstCombinerImpl declaration in InstCombineInternal.h
Behavioral change: Recognizes multiplication/division comparison forms using signed division in addition to the prior unsigned-only forms.; Changes the generated overflow intrinsic from unconditionally llvm.umul.with.overflow to llvm.umul.with.overflow or llvm.smul.with.overflow according to the matched division opcode.; Broadens InstCombine matching for ICmp expressions involving multiplication and division, including signed arithmetic.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: The retrieved evidence does not show the PR49535 C reproducer or its exact failing IR pattern.; The change affects arithmetic ICmp simplification that can execute during -O2 InstCombine processing.

steps.subject: [InstCombine] C - ctpop(a) - > ctpop(~a)) if C is bitwidth (PR50104)

evidence: Adds a narrow ctpop subtraction identity in InstCombine.
The rewrite does not invoke ValueTracking or interact with generic arithmetic invertibility beyond broad shared-pass overlap.
features: ctpop, instcombine, intrinsic-canonicalization, meta:core-llvm, one-use-match, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This InstCombine change adds a visitSub canonicalization for the identity bitwidth - ctpop(X) = ctpop(~X). When the left operand is exactly the scalar bit width and the ctpop call has one use, the subtraction is replaced with a ctpop intrinsic on the bitwise complement of the original argument.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitSub; sub_ctpop; sub_ctpop_vec; ctpop1_multiuse
Behavioral change: Recognizes C - ctpop(X) when C equals the scalar bit width of the result type.; Requires the ctpop intrinsic to have one use before applying the rewrite.; Replaces the subtraction with ctpop(not X), including for the tested vector form.; Introduces a new xor/not operation and a replacement ctpop call while eliminating the matching subtraction.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is shared with the reported trace.; No ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, or BO1->getOperand occurrence is shown in the changed implementation.
Reproducer link: The added coverage is limited to ctpop subtraction identities, including scalar, vector, and multi-use cases.; No compact C reproducer, optimizer crash test, or ValueTracking assertion test is added by this commit.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine
Causal explanation: The candidate modifies InstCombine arithmetic canonicalization and can expose a different instruction graph, namely xor followed by ctpop instead of subtraction from ctpop. That shared-pass relationship is the only evidence-backed connection to PR49535. The issue signal concerns invertible-operand reasoning around ValueTracking, whereas this hunk only matches a narrow ctpop identity and contains no shown ValueTracking query, making a direct causal connection weak.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: The implementation change is accompanied by scalar and vector InstCombine tests.; The one-use matcher constrains the new transform and avoids rewriting the explicitly tested extra-use case.; No build-system, public-header, or API changes are visible in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes the InstCombine fold that rewrote comparisons of a shifted value against zero into unsigned range comparisons on the unshifted input. In particular, zero equality and non-equality cases handled by foldICmpShrConstant no longer produce ICMP_ULT or ICMP_UGT comparisons involving X and a shift-derived constant; the original comparison of the shift result is retained.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant; lshr_eq_0_multiuse; lshr_ne_0_multiuse; ashr_eq_0_multiuse; with_range
Behavioral change: Removes the C.isNullValue() rewrite for shifted comparisons.; Stops lowering shifted-value == 0 into an unsigned-less-than comparison on the source value.; Stops lowering the corresponding non-equality case into an unsigned-greater-than comparison on the source value.; Leaves multi-use lshr and ashr zero comparisons in terms of the shifted result rather than replacing them with source-value range checks.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is shared with the reported trace.; No direct ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, or BO1->getOperand reference is present in the candidate implementation hunk.
Reproducer link: The updated tests specifically cover multi-use lshr/ashr comparisons against zero.; The supplied issue context does not establish that the PR49535 testcase contains this exact shifted-zero-comparison pattern.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine
Causal explanation: This is an indirect but plausible candidate because it changes the arithmetic and comparison IR shape produced by InstCombine: downstream reasoning sees a comparison of a shift result instead of a range comparison on the input. Such a shape change could alter later ValueTracking queries within InstCombine. However, the retrieved change neither calls nor modifies getInvertibleOperand or ValueTracking, and it contains no assertion reproducer, so the causal link is not direct.
Causal confidence: 0.28
Build risk: Implementation and InstCombine regression-test expectations are changed together.; No build-system, public-header, or API changes are visible in the retrieved hunks.; The commit is a revert, so it removes an existing optimization rather than introducing a new implementation path.

The removed logic created an assumption that the argument was null and erased the free call; after the revert, those free calls are retained.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitFree
Behavioral change: Stops deriving an argument-is-null assumption from nofree attributes when that argument is passed to free.; Stops emitting llvm.assume for the inferred null condition.; Stops erasing the free call for the affected nofree-attribute cases.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This ValueTracking change extends getInvertibleOperand to handle pairs of PHI nodes that are simple recurrences in the same block. It recognizes when both recurrences apply the same invertible binary step to their respective starts, maps the invertible operand back to the PHI start operand according to incoming-edge order, and enables isKnownNonEqual to prove corresponding add, subtract, and multiply recurrences unequal.
Changed symbols: getInvertibleOperand; isKnownNonEqual; matchSimpleRecurrence; PHINode recurrence handling in getInvertibleOperand; recurrence_add_neq; recurrence_sub_neq; recurrence_mul_neq
Behavioral change: getInvertibleOperand now accepts PHI-node pairs representing simple recurrences, provided both PHIs are in the same block and both recurrence steps match.; It recursively asks getInvertibleOperand about the recurrence update BinaryOperators and only proceeds when the returned invertible operand index is zero.; It asserts that the selected BinaryOperator operand is the corresponding PHI, then returns the PHI incoming operand index containing the recurrence start value.; ValueTracking can consequently fold equality checks between the tested unequal recurrences to false, as shown by the updated analysis tests.
Assertion or trace link: ValueTracking; getInvertibleOperand; assert(BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2); BO1->getOperand; PHINode; matchSimpleRecurrence
Reproducer link: The added recurrence_add_neq, recurrence_sub_neq, and recurrence_mul_neq tests create PHI recurrences and cause their comparisons to be simplified to false.; The retrieved tests do not establish that the issue's compact C testcase has the same recurrence structure, but they exercise the newly added recurrence path directly.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Analysis/ValueTracking; isKnownNonEqual
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate because it directly adds the getInvertibleOperand PHI-recurrence path and the exact BO1->getOperand assertion shape identified in the issue signal. An invalid correspondence between the recursively selected invertible operand and the recurrence PHI would trip this newly introduced assertion. The hunk does not prove that the reported C testcase reaches this path, but it is direct source-level evidence for the reported assertion family.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit generalizes InstCombine's multiplication-overflow-check folding from unsigned division patterns to handle signed division as well. +; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[B]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[B_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[A_IV]], 1

+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label [[LOOP]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RES:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[A_IV]], [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[RES]]
+;
+entry:
+  %B = add i8 %A, 1
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%iv.next, %loop]

+  %B.iv = phi i8 [%B, %entry], [%B.iv.next, %loop]
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
+  %A.iv.next = add i8 %A.iv, 1
+  %B.iv.next = add i8 %B.iv, 2

@@ -442,0 +443,54 @@ unreachable:
+; Was pr49856.  We can match the recurrence without a loop
+; since dominance collapses in unreachable code.  Conceptually,
+; this is a recurrence which only executes one iteration.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647)
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence
+;
+bb:
+  br label %bb1
+
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %bb
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  ret void
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+
+; Tweak of pr49856 test case - analogous, but there is a loop
+; it's trip count simply doesn't relate to the single iteration
+; "recurrence" we found.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence_2() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence_2'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: <multiple exits> Unpredictable backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable max backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable predicated backedge-taken count.
+;
+bb:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  br label %bb1
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %loop
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  br label %loop
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+

+  %0 = bitcast i32* %x_on_stack to i8*
+  call void @use(i8* %0)

+  ret void

+  ret void

diff --git a/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll b/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll
index 0b9525ddf4ed..962252559af1 100644
--- a/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll
+++ b/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll
@@ -442,0 +443,54 @@ unreachable:
+; Was pr49856.  We can match the recurrence without a loop
+; since dominance collapses in unreachable code.  Conceptually,
+; this is a recurrence which only executes one iteration.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647)
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence
+;
+bb:
+  br label %bb1
+
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %bb
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  ret void
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+
+; Tweak of pr49856 test case - analogous, but there is a loop
+; it's trip count simply doesn't relate to the single iteration
+; "recurrence" we found.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence_2() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence_2'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: <multiple exits> Unpredictable backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable max backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable predicated backedge-taken count.
+;
+bb:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  br label %bb1
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %loop
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  br label %loop
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+

--- a/llvm/test/Analysis/ValueTracking/known-non-equal.ll
+++ b/llvm/test/Analysis/ValueTracking/known-non-equal.ll
@@ -687,0 +688,109 @@ exit:
+; If the steps are different, the invertibility is not enough
+; (Though, in this case, we could prove neq with different logic)
+define i1 @recurrence_add_diff_step(i8 %A) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @recurrence_add_diff_step(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B:%.*]] = add i8 [[A:%.*]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ], [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[A]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[A_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[B]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[B_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[A_IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[B_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label [[LOOP]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RES:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[A_IV]], [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[RES]]
+;
+entry:
+  %B = add i8 %A, 1
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%iv.next, %loop]
+  %A.iv = phi i8 [%A, %entry], [%A.iv.next, %loop]
+  %B.iv = phi i8 [%B, %entry], [%B.iv.next, %loop]
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
+  %A.iv.next = add i8 %A.iv, 1
+  %B.iv.next = add i8 %B.iv, 2
+  %cmp = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit
+exit:
+  %res = icmp eq i8 %A.iv, %B.iv
+  ret i1 %res
+}
+
+; We currently require recursion through first operand
+; (Though for add, which is cummutable, we could support either)
+define i1 @recurrence_add_op_order(i8 %A) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @recurrence_add_op_order(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B:%.*]] = add i8 [[A:%.*]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:

diff --git a/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll b/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll
index 0b9525ddf4ed..962252559af1 100644
--- a/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll
+++ b/llvm/test/Analysis/ScalarEvolution/shift-recurrences.ll
@@ -442,0 +443,54 @@ unreachable:
+; Was pr49856.  We can match the recurrence without a loop
+; since dominance collapses in unreachable code.  Conceptually,
+; this is a recurrence which only executes one iteration.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647)
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence
+;
+bb:
+  br label %bb1
+
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %bb
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  ret void
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+
+; Tweak of pr49856 test case - analogous, but there is a loop
+; it's trip count simply doesn't relate to the single iteration
+; "recurrence" we found.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence_2() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence_2'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: <multiple exits> Unpredictable backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable max backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable predicated backedge-taken count.
+;
+bb:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  br label %bb1
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %loop
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  br label %loop
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+

+  %V128 = shufflevector <2 x i64> %src128, <2 x i64> undef, <2 x i32> <i32 1, i32 0>

+

+; CHECK-NEXT:  Cost Model: Found an estimated cost of 18 for instruction: %V128 = shufflevector <4 x float> %src128, <4 x float> undef, <4 x i32> <i32 3, i32 2, i32 1, i32 0>
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Cost Model: Found an estimated cost of 0 for instruction: ret void
+;
+  %V64 = shufflevector <2 x float> %src64, <2 x float> undef, <2 x i32> <i32 1, i32 0>
+  %V128 = shufflevector <4 x float> %src128, <4 x float> undef, <4 x i32> <i32 3, i32 2, i32 1, i32 0>

+;
+  %V128 = shufflevector <2 x double> %src128, <2 x double> undef, <2 x i32> <i32 1, i32 0>

+; If the steps are different, the invertibility is not enough

+define i1 @recurrence_add_diff_step(i8 %A) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @recurrence_add_diff_step(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B:%.*]] = add i8 [[A:%.*]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ], [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[A]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[A_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[B]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[B_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[A_IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[B_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label [[LOOP]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RES:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[A_IV]], [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[RES]]
+;
+entry:
+  %B = add i8 %A, 1
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%iv.next, %loop]
+  %A.iv = phi i8 [%A, %entry], [%A.iv.next, %loop]
+  %B.iv = phi i8 [%B, %entry], [%B.iv.next, %loop]
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
+  %A.iv.next = add i8 %A.iv, 1
+  %B.iv.next = add i8 %B.iv, 2
+  %cmp = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit
+exit:
+  %res = icmp eq i8 %A.iv, %B.iv
+  ret i1 %res
+}
+
+; We currently require recursion through first operand
+; (Though for add, which is cummutable, we could support either)
+define i1 @recurrence_add_op_order(i8 %A) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @recurrence_add_op_order(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B:%.*]] = add i8 [[A:%.*]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ], [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[A]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[A_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[B]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[B_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 1, [[A_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 1, [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label [[LOOP]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RES:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[A_IV]], [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[RES]]
+;
+entry:
+  %B = add i8 %A, 1
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%iv.next, %loop]
+  %A.iv = phi i8 [%A, %entry], [%A.iv.next, %loop]
+  %B.iv = phi i8 [%B, %entry], [%B.iv.next, %loop]
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1

+  %B.iv.next = add i8 1, %B.iv
+  %cmp = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 10

+  ret i1 %res
+}

+; RUN: opt -O2 -pass-remarks-analysis=openmp-opt -enable-new-pm < %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=MODULE
+target datalayout = "e-i64:64-i128:128-v16:16-v32:32-n16:32:64"
+
+@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [13 x i8] c"Alloc Shared\00", align 1
+
+; MODULE: remark: openmp_opt_module.c:5:7: Found thread data sharing on the GPU. Expect degraded performance due to data globalization.
+
+define void @foo() {
+entry:
+  %x = call i8* @__kmpc_data_sharing_push_stack(i64 4, i16 0), !dbg !7
+  %x_on_stack = bitcast i8* %x to i32*
+  %0 = bitcast i32* %x_on_stack to i8*
+  call void @use(i8* %0)
+  call void @__kmpc_data_sharing_pop_stack(i8* %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+define void @use(i8* %0) {
+entry:
+  %.addr = alloca i8*, align 8
+  store i8* %0, i8** %.addr, align 8
+  ret void
+}
+
+define internal i8* @__kmpc_data_sharing_push_stack(i64 %DataSize, i16 %shared) {
+entry:
+  %call = call i8* @_Z10SafeMallocmPKc(i64 %DataSize, i8* getelementptr inbounds ([13 x i8], [13 x i8]* @.str, i64 0, i64 0)) #11
+  ret i8* %call
+}
+
+; Function Attrs: convergent nounwind mustprogress
+declare i8* @_Z10SafeMallocmPKc(i64 %size, i8* nocapture readnone %msg)
+
+declare void @__kmpc_data_sharing_pop_stack(i8*)
+
+!llvm.dbg.cu = !{!0}
+!llvm.module.flags = !{!3, !4}
+
+!0 = distinct !DICompileUnit(language: DW_LANG_C99, file: !1, producer: "clang version 12.0.0", isOptimized: false, runtimeVersion: 0, emissionKind: FullDebug, enums: !2, splitDebugInlining: false, nameTableKind: None)

+!2 = !{}
+!3 = !{i32 2, !"Debug Info Version", i32 3}
+!4 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
+!5 = distinct !DISubprogram(name: "foo", scope: !1, file: !1, line: 1, type: !6, scopeLine: 1, flags: DIFlagPrototyped, spFlags: DISPFlagDefinition | DISPFlagOptimized, unit: !0, retainedNodes: !2)

@@ -442,0 +443,54 @@ unreachable:
+; Was pr49856.  We can match the recurrence without a loop
+; since dominance collapses in unreachable code.  Conceptually,
+; this is a recurrence which only executes one iteration.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647)
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence
+;
+bb:
+  br label %bb1
+
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %bb
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  ret void
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+
+; Tweak of pr49856 test case - analogous, but there is a loop
+; it's trip count simply doesn't relate to the single iteration
+; "recurrence" we found.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence_2() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence_2'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: <multiple exits> Unpredictable backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable max backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable predicated backedge-taken count.
+;
+bb:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  br label %bb1
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %loop
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  br label %loop
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+

+; CHECK-LABEL: @recurrence_add_diff_step(

+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ], [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[B]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[B_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[A_IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 [[B_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label [[LOOP]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RES:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[A_IV]], [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[RES]]
+;
+entry:
+  %B = add i8 %A, 1
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%iv.next, %loop]
+  %A.iv = phi i8 [%A, %entry], [%A.iv.next, %loop]
+  %B.iv = phi i8 [%B, %entry], [%B.iv.next, %loop]
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
+  %A.iv.next = add i8 %A.iv, 1
+  %B.iv.next = add i8 %B.iv, 2
+  %cmp = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit
+exit:
+  %res = icmp eq i8 %A.iv, %B.iv
+  ret i1 %res
+}

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[B]], [[ENTRY]] ], [ [[B_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP]] ]

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[A_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 1, [[A_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[B_IV_NEXT]] = add i8 1, [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label [[LOOP]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RES:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[A_IV]], [[B_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i1 [[RES]]
+;
+entry:
+  %B = add i8 %A, 1
+  br label %loop
+loop:

+  %A.iv = phi i8 [%A, %entry], [%A.iv.next, %loop]
+  %B.iv = phi i8 [%B, %entry], [%B.iv.next, %loop]

+  call void @use(i8* %0)

+bb:

+

+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  ret void
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1

+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence_2

+bb:

top_candidates.subject: Look through invertible recurrences in isKnownNonEqual
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends ValueTracking's getInvertibleOperand logic to reason through pairs of PHI-node simple recurrences for isKnownNonEqual. The new PHI case extracts each recurrence's binary update and start/step values, recursively checks whether the update operators are invertible with respect to operand 0, and maps the recurrence result back to the corresponding PHI incoming operand. It also adds direct assertions that the recursively selected binary-operator operand is the recurrence PHI.
Changed symbols: getInvertibleOperand; isKnownNonEqual; matchSimpleRecurrence; recurrence_add_neq; recurrence_sub_neq; recurrence_mul_neq
Behavioral change: Adds handling for Instruction::PHI operands in getInvertibleOperand when both values are simple recurrences in the same loop block.; Recursively evaluates the recurrence update BinaryOperators and only accepts cases where their invertible operand index is 0.; Introduces assertions that BO1->getOperand(*Idx) equals PN1 and BO2->getOperand(*Idx) equals PN2 before selecting the corresponding PHI start-value operand.; Allows isKnownNonEqual-based simplification to prove unequal add, subtract, and multiply recurrences unequal, as reflected by tests changing an equality comparison result to constant false.
Assertion or trace link: getInvertibleOperand; ValueTracking; BO1->getOperand; assert(BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2)
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O2 Clang crash caused by a ValueTracking assertion around getInvertibleOperand.; This change adds a new getInvertibleOperand path specifically for PHI recurrences and adds the BO1->getOperand assertion form named in the issue signal.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Analysis; ValueTracking; isKnownNonEqual; InstCombine consumers of ValueTracking at -O2
Causal explanation: This is a direct high-risk match: the candidate modifies the exact ValueTracking helper named by the crash and introduces assertions over BO1->getOperand in its new PHI-recurrence path. A compact optimized testcase containing recurrence PHIs could reach this path through isKnownNonEqual/InstCombine and violate the newly assumed operand-position invariant. The included tests demonstrate intended recurrence simplification but do not cover assertion safety for differing recurrence operand layouts.
Causal confidence: 0.98
Build risk: Implementation change is confined to ValueTracking and has matching ValueTracking regression-test updates.; The added assertions create debug/assert-enabled crash risk for recurrence shapes not satisfying the assumed operand-0 layout.; No dedicated regression test for the reported assertion failure is visible in the retrieved hunks.

Summary: This libc++ test change makes an unordered-map local-iterator debug-mode test reliably operate on a non-empty bucket: it inserts key 42, finds that key's bucket, begins iteration in that bucket, and verifies the iterator is initially not at the bucket end before testing increment behavior. The change is test-only and does not alter LLVM or Clang optimizer implementation.
Changed symbols: main; C::local_iterator; C::size_type; std::make_pair; std::string
Behavioral change: Changes the test setup from constructing a container with one bucket and beginning bucket 0 to inserting an element and selecting the bucket containing that element.; Adds an explicit precondition check that the local iterator is not equal to the selected bucket's end iterator before increment testing.; Does not change compiler optimization, ValueTracking invertibility analysis, or InstCombine behavior.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends ValueTracking's getInvertibleOperand logic to recognize pairs of PHI nodes representing simple recurrences in the same loop. It recursively determines whether their recurrence update operations are invertible, maps the inferred recurrence operand back to the PHI incoming value, and enables isKnownNonEqual-driven folding of comparisons between add, subtract, and multiply recurrences to false.
Changed symbols: getInvertibleOperand; matchSimpleRecurrence; PHINode; recurrence_add_neq; recurrence_sub_neq; recurrence_mul_neq
Behavioral change: getInvertibleOperand now handles Instruction::PHI by matching two PHI nodes as simple recurrences, requiring that they belong to the same parent block, and recursively analyzing their BinaryOperator recurrence updates.; The new PHI path accepts only a recursive result whose invertible operand index is 0, then returns the PHI incoming-value index corresponding to the recurrence start value.; The implementation adds assertions that the recursively selected BinaryOperator operand is the corresponding recurrence PHI and that matching PHI incoming operands contain the recurrence update.; ValueTracking tests now expect comparisons of unequal add, subtract, and multiply recurrences to be folded directly to false rather than emitted as runtime icmp instructions.
Assertion or trace link: ValueTracking; getInvertibleOperand; BO1->getOperand; assert(BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2)
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O2 compiler crash in a compact C testcase.; The new code specifically analyzes loop PHI recurrences and their BinaryOperator updates, a shape that can be reached while optimizing loop-derived arithmetic.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Analysis/ValueTracking; isKnownNonEqual; InstCombine/optimization clients of ValueTracking

The new recursive operand-index reasoning assumes that an inferred index of 0 identifies the recurrence PHI; if that relationship does not hold for an encountered recurrence pair, the newly added assertion can fire.
